what: A pen carried by a moving robot leaves a trace of its actual path. The trailing pen traces the geometry of motion and turning.
try: Reset to clear the ink and run the drawing program.
Change one wheel speed or distance, Reset and compare the resulting curve.
why: The pen follows a point attached to the chassis. If that point is offset from the drive axle, turning the chassis also sweeps the pen around the axle.
matters: Tool placement matters when robots draw, weld or inspect a surface.
question: Do the pen and drive-axle midpoint always draw the same path?
answer: No. An offset point follows a different arc during a turn, even though both belong to one rigid chassis.
further: Compare wheel-path drawing with rotating-paper drawing.
Predict the effect of moving a pen farther from the axle.
